title: How to Do a Proper Glute Bridge at Home
intro: The glute bridge trains your butt and back thigh muscles while you lie down, so it's beginner-friendly and gentle on the knees. Very suitable if you sit a lot at the office or in the car.
muscles: Glutes, hamstrings and core. Honest note: this exercise strengthens your glutes and thighs, but it doesn't burn fat from that specific area. Fat goes down from the whole body through eating and daily movement.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Bring your heels closer to your butt until your fingers can almost touch your heels.
Place your hands by your sides and tighten your tummy slightly.
Press your heels into the floor and lift your hips until your shoulders, hips and knees form a straight line.
Squeeze your glutes and hold for 1-2 seconds at the top.
mistakes: Lifting too high until your lower back arches. Stop when your body is straight. Squeeze your glutes, don't arch your back.
Feet too far away, so your hamstrings cramp quickly. Bring your heels a bit closer to your butt.
Going fast without squeezing. Hold for a moment at the top so your glutes really work.
easier: Lift only halfway and do fewer reps.
harder: Hold for 5 seconds at the top of every rep, put your feet on the sofa, or try a single-leg glute bridge (one leg straightened).
dose: 2-3 sets x 10-15 reps, rest 45-60 seconds. Do it 3 times a week.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your lower back or hips. If you have long-lasting back pain, see a doctor or physiotherapist before continuing.

faq.q: Why do I feel it in my hamstrings or lower back, not my glutes?
faq.a: Usually because your feet are too far away or you're lifting too high. Bring your heels closer, press them into the floor and squeeze your glutes before lifting.

faq.q: Can glute bridges lift or shape my butt?
faq.a: They strengthen your glute muscles, but everyone's body shape is different and depends a lot on genetics, eating and consistency. We can't promise specific results, but strong glutes are really good for posture and daily movement.

faq.q: I have lower back pain. Can I do this?
faq.a: Many people feel comfortable with glute bridges, but start with small, slow lifts. If the pain gets worse, stop and get advice from a doctor or physio.
